slots.hypothesis: Core: day_durbin_watson(Volume). In this library the denominator is Σx², so the value is about 2(1−ρ₁)·CV²/(1+CV²). A high value means volume comes in isolated, attention-driven spikes. A low value means smooth, persistent flow from sliced meta-orders. It is the only subtree in M batch 1 that survives multiple testing (+0.76, p≈0.0002, in 46 of 95 candidates). All 46 peripheries seen so far are either monotone pow wraps or cross_cov against a 30-day median, and those wraps give the same signal under rank. The new peripheries are: (a) within-stock normalization (cross_zscore, cross_madz, ts_rank, and a recent EMA measured against its own 120 days); (b) ranking inside deciles with cs_bucket_rank, by day_gini(Volume) to isolate the persistence half, by ListAge to remove thin new listings piling up at DW≈2, and by 20-day amount for interaction-level liquidity neutralization; (c) direction, via DW × net-buy share and rolling correlation with the day's return and volume; (d) the 20-day distribution (q75 tail mean, std, 30-day median). Out-of-sample case: these remove the level/interaction confounds the polynomial control residuals cannot remove, which are the likely cause of the batch's train/valid sign instability. 15 seeds.

Price direction in the heavy-volume minutes. Returns realized in volume-burst minutes are mostly liquidity demand and should reverse (Campbell–Grossman–Wang 1993, Admati–Pfleiderer 1988). Returns in quiet minutes are closer to information and should persist (Llorente et al. 2002). Implementation: burst-minute return day_topw_mean(Ret, in_madz(Volume,30)), raw and minus day_mean(Ret), and ranked within deciles of the 20-day mean minute return. Also volume-weighted minus equal-weighted minute return, day_corr(Ret, Volume) and its lead/lag versions, VWAP/TWAP, day_corr(Close, Volume), net-buy share given the price move, and a 1-week vs 60-day z-score, all averaged over 20 days. Why it is new: no candidate in M batch 1 combines minute returns and minute volume. The signal is signed and built to be orthogonal to the 20-day total-return control, because it measures how that return is split between burst and quiet minutes. 15 seeds.
